description: Clarification decision suite, label-widening revision of clarification-v1 (2026-10-25). Items, questions, expected behaviors, histories, answer keywords and forbidden terms are IDENTICAL to v1 - only caveatKeywords on two clarify items were widened to phrasing-robust discriminators of the same missing detail (cl-conflict-001 also accepts the guidance/runbook/30s/300s vocabulary a correct follow-up naturally uses; cl-amb-002 also accepts the candidate-symptom vocabulary). Observed-behavior comparisons across v1/v2 datasets remain apples-to-apples.

items.question: Our API has become really slow lately. How do I fix it?
items.expectedAnswer: No component named — the KB maps slow-API symptoms onto at least three different fixes (Node.js event-loop blocking, Postgres pool exhaustion, Redis latency). A correct response asks ONE question naming the candidate components (e.g. 'Which component is slow — the Node.js API, PostgreSQL or Redis?') instead of picking one. Abstention is acceptable.

items.question: Redis is struggling in production. Which settings should we change?
items.expectedAnswer: 'Struggling' is undefined: the KB Redis doc covers eviction storms/data loss, OOM write rejections and cache stampedes — with different fixes per symptom. A correct response asks what symptom is actually happening (one targeted question) before recommending eviction policy, maxmemory or TTL changes. Abstention is acceptable.

items.question: Nginx is returning 502 for some requests. What should I change in the config?
items.expectedAnswer: A 502 has three distinct root causes in the KB (connect refused = upstream down, timed out reading header = slow endpoint, prematurely closed = keepalive mismatch), each with a different config fix. A correct response asks which failure signature the Nginx error log shows, naming the candidates, instead of changing an arbitrary directive. Abstention is acceptable.

items.question: How big should we set the Node.js heap for our service?
items.expectedAnswer: The KB rule sizes the heap relative to the container memory limit (heap ≈ 60–75% of the limit; 384 for a 512 MB container) — without the container limit no number can be correct. A correct response asks how much memory the container is allowed (one question) before giving a value. Abstention is acceptable.

items.question: It's failing with the same error as yesterday again. Walk me through the fix.
items.expectedAnswer: The question refers to an error and an incident ('yesterday') that are unavailable — there is no prior conversation and the KB cannot know them. A correct response asks which error/component is involved (e.g. 'Which error are you seeing? Could you paste it?') instead of guessing a component. Abstention is acceptable.

items.question: What value should we set statement_timeout to on the cluster?
items.expectedAnswer: AMBIGUOUS + CONFLICTING EVIDENCE: retrieval surfaces two contradictory KB documents — the incident report recommends a global 30s cap, the newer runbook (which supersedes it) recommends a global 300s with per-role overrides (30s OLTP / 120s workers). The right value depends on the workload and role, which the question does not state. A correct response asks which workload/role the timeout is for (OLTP API vs reporting/batch) instead of adopting one document blindly; it must NOT present either number as the unconditional answer. Abstention is acceptable.

items.question: Got it. So what heap cap should we set for that Node.js container?

history.content: Our Node.js API container keeps getting OOM-killed. Exit code 137, docker inspect shows OOMKilled: true, and the container has a 512 MB memory limit.

The kernel is killing the container because Node sizes its old-space heap from the host's memory by default, not the container limit. Cap the V8 heap explicitly below the container limit and verify with v8.getHeapStatistics().heap_size_limit [1].

items.expectedAnswer: APPEARS ambiguous in isolation (no container limit stated) but the conversation history supplies the 512 MB limit — the assistant must use it and answer with the concrete cap: heap ≈ 60–75% of the container limit, i.e. NODE_OPTIONS=--max-old-space-size=384 for a 512 MB container. Asking 'which container?' again would be an unnecessary clarification.

items.question: Which Nginx directive should I change first to fix these 502s, and what does it do?

history.content: Nginx returns 502 Bad Gateway intermittently. The error log shows 'upstream prematurely closed connection' while reading the response.
That signature means the upstream closed the connection mid-response — classically an app restart or an idle-keepalive mismatch between Nginx and the app, not a slow endpoint [1].

items.expectedAnswer: In isolation 'these 502s' is an unresolvable reference; the history pins the failure signature ('upstream prematurely closed connection'), so the correct response answers with the matching fix — enable upstream keepalive (proxy_http_version 1.1 with proxy_set_header Connection "") instead of re-asking which 502 flavor it is.

items.question: Our Node.js container dies with exit code 137 and docker inspect reports OOMKilled: true. The container memory limit is 512 MB. How do we stop the restarts?
items.expectedAnswer: Fully specified (symptom, error code, container limit): cap the V8 heap below the container limit — NODE_OPTIONS=--max-old-space-size=384 for a 512 MB container (heap ≈ 60–75% rule) — plus size headroom from measured peak usage. No clarification is needed; asking one would be unnecessary.

items.question: Postgres reports 'ERROR: deadlock detected (SQLSTATE 40P01)' when two batch jobs update overlapping rows. How do we stop the deadlocks?
items.expectedAnswer: Fully specified (exact SQLSTATE, trigger): impose a consistent global lock order (sort ids before updating / SELECT ... FOR UPDATE ORDER BY), keep transactions short, and retry on 40P01 with jittered backoff. No clarification is needed.

items.question: Turn on the PostgreSQL slow query log with a 500 ms threshold, and then set up pg_stat_statements so we can rank queries by total time.
items.expectedAnswer: PARTIAL: the slow log part is covered (logging_collector, log_min_duration_statement = '500ms', log_line_prefix) — the pg_stat_statements part is explicitly NOT covered by the KB (the doc says it is a separate tool with its own runbook). Honest answer: give the logging config with citations and state that pg_stat_statements setup is not in the knowledge base.

items.question: Configure Nginx rate limiting to 10 requests per second per client IP on /login, and also send a Slack alert whenever a client gets rate-limited.
items.expectedAnswer: PARTIAL: the rate limiting part is covered (limit_req_zone with rate=10r/s keyed on $binary_remote_addr, limit_req_status 429) — Slack alerting / notification integrations are NOT covered by the KB. Honest answer: give the rate limiting config with citations and state the Slack part is not in the knowledge base.

items.question: How do I rotate the TLS certificates on our Kubernetes ingress controller?
items.expectedAnswer: Kubernetes/ingress/TLS rotation is not covered by the knowledge base at all. Correct behavior: refuse with an explicit not-covered admission (or the retrieval gate abstains) — never a fabricated cert-manager walkthrough.

items.question: What's a good weekly gym plan to prepare for a marathon?
items.expectedAnswer: Off-topic fitness question — the retrieval gate should reject it outright (sufficient=false, no LLM call).
